sentences.text: Shri V.K. Jha, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri R.S. Yadav, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondents/State.

This criminal appeal under Section 14 (A) (2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (hereinafter referred to as "SC/ST Act") has been filed by the appellant assailing the order dated 15.05.2024 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Shivpuri (M.P.) whereby,
application preferred by the appellant herein under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. relating to Crime No. 67 of 2024 registered at Police Station Indar, District Shivpuri (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 376(1), 341, 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w) (ii) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act has been rejected.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further argued that MLC report does not indicate any injury.
It is a case of consensual relationship.
He is in custody since 05.04.2024.The appellant is a poor agriculturist.
Further incarceration will cause hardship to his family.
The appellant has no criminal antecedents and he is permanent resident of District Shivpuri (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Hence, he prays for grant of bail to the appellant.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the appeal and prayed for its rejection.

application preferred by the appellant herein under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. relating to Crime No. 67 of 2024 registered at Police Station Indar, District Shivpuri (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 376(1), 341, 506 of IPC and Sections 3(1)(w) (ii) and 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act has been rejected.
Learned counsel for the appellant argued that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
He is in custody since 05.04.2024.The appellant is a poor agriculturist.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting upon the merits of the case, this appeal stands allowed and it is 2 CRA-6811-2024 directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Committal Court.
This order will remain operative subject to compliance of the following conditions by the appellant:-
1. The appellant will comply with all the terms and conditions of the bond executed by him;
2. The appellant will cooperate in the investigation/trial, as the case may be;
